_comment: KNOWN-GAP REPRODUCTION (A) for layout/erc/adc_block.supply-spec.json's
`ties[]` omission. Not an item-11 artifact -- never cite this run as
evidence about this block.
Byte-identical to the supply spec except for the `ties[]` entry below:
the only form of well-tie declaration this stream can express, a BARE
`tap_layer` naming COMP 22/0 with no `tap_requires` narrowing.
EXPECTED OUTCOME: `klt erc` classifies the tie as DEGENERATE
(klayout-tools#2199) and records its `erc.missing_tie` work in
`erc_coverage.skipped` with reason `degenerate_tap_declaration`,
downgrading `erc_status` from `clean` to `clean_partial`. It does NOT
report a clean well-tie verdict, and it does not report findings.
WHY: a bare COMP tap layer matches every source/drain contact inside
the well, not just the taps, so any of them reaching `vdd` would make
the well look tied. The narrowing that would fix it -- `COMP n Nplus`,
the real gf180mcu tap boolean -- has nothing to intersect, because
this generated full-custom stream draws no implant layers at all (see
reproduction B, adc_block.tie-narrowed.known-gap.json).
This case is committed so the supply spec's `ties[]` omission is a
MEASURED conclusion with a re-runnable artifact behind it, not an
assertion. `run_erc.py` re-runs it and asserts the outcome above.
